To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a new solid superacid catalyst, SnO2/SO42− (H0≤−16.4), was synthesized from tin oxide and sulfuric acid, which was used as a solid catalyst for the isomerization of n-butane to isobutylenes at room temperature.

a solid superacid catalyst of SO42−-SnO2 with an acid strength Ho≤−16, which is the highest among solid superacids, was successfully synthesized and its catalytic activity was confirmed for the skeletal isomeration of n-butane to isobutyane.

the solid superacid of SO42-/SnO2 with acid strength of Ho ≤−16.04 has been prepared from tin hydroxides obtained from solutions of different pH by the treatment with H2SO4, and the solid superacid is active for the skeletal transformation of butane to iso-butane at room temperature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of a solid superacid catalyst of SO42− /SnO2 with an acid strength as high as Ho≤−16.
the preparation and characterization of a new solid superacid of SO42- /SnO2 with an acid strength as high as Ho≤−16.04.
the synthesis of solid superacid with an acid strength Ho≤−16, which was obtained by calcination in the air at 823 K of tin hydroxide obtained by the reaction of tin oxide with water.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the solid superacid of SO42-/SnO2 was prepared for the first time, which was active for the isomerization of n-butane to isobute at room temperature.
the solid superacid SO42−/ SnO2 was synthesized from the solution with a high pH value, and it has a high acid strength and is active for the isomerization of n-butane to isobute.

the acid strength of the solid superacid of SO42-/SnO2 is stronger than that of the solid superacids of SbF5/SiO2, SbF5/Al2O3, SbF5/SO4/SiO2 and H3PO4/HF/Al2O2, but is weaker than that of the liquid superacids of HSO3F·SbF5 and HSO3F/FSO3H/SbF
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the solid superacid of SO42-/SnO2 with acid strength of Ho ≤ −16.04 was prepared from the tin hydroxide obtained from the solution of tin chloride with pH=10 and the acid strength of the superacid was estimated to be −16.04 by using the method of Hammett indicator.
the acid strength of the solid superacid of SO42-/SnO2 was found to be Ho≤−16, which was the highest value ever reported for the solid superacids.

the superacidity of SnO2/SO4−2 was generated by the strong interaction between the surface oxygen atoms of SnO2 and the sulfate groups, which were formed by the adsorption of sulfuric acid on the surface of SnO2.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the acid strength of solid superacids can be increased by the use of tin hydroxide as a precursor, which is a cheap and abundant material, rather than the use of expensive tin oxide or metal tin as precursors.

a solid superacid can be prepared from a metal hydroxide by the following procedure: (1) preparation of the metal hydroxide from an aqueous solution with a pH of 10; (2) exposure to sulfuric acid; (3) calcination in air; (4) exposure to a strong base; (5) calcination in nitrogen.
the acid strength of the solid SO42−/TiO2 catalyst can be enhanced by the calcination of the catalyst precursor in air at high temperature.
